title: IBM BPM and process automation tools

videos.script: Serra Alta runs three of its processes on a product most of its staff have never heard of. {{estate}} A new farm joins. A distributor asks for thirty days to pay. A supplier sends its certificates. Each of those is an instance of a process, and something has to keep track of it for days. {{engine}} At Serra Alta that something is IBM BPM, installed in 2014. One developer still knows how it works. This lesson is about what a tool like that is made of, and what owning one means. {{suite}} First the parts: a modeller, an engine, a task list for people, forms, and calls to other systems. Then the market around it. Large suites, open engines, low-code flows, and robots that type into screens. {{map}} Then the hard part, which is time. A farm takes a month to join. Change the process halfway, and the old instances are still running on the old one. {{versions}} Last, the bill. Licences, scarce skills, upgrades, and the price of leaving. Joana sets out to write a short note saying the suite should go. The note she ends up writing is longer, and it says something else. {{assessment}}
